title: Retrieval Drift Regression Benchmark Pack
description: Regression cases for focused coding prompts that previously drifted toward project-meta notes or unrelated implementation domains.

tasks.title: BSQ Full Implementation Request Must Stay on BSQ
tasks.objective: Measure whether a focused BSQ coding request stays on the BSQ problem instead of drifting into unrelated sample projects or generic system-design content.
tasks.prompt: Generate a full BSQ implementation in C: explain architecture, modules, execution flow, edge cases, and provide the main code skeleton.
expected_signals: describes dynamic programming or square selection
describes output or marking the biggest square
anti_signals: focuses on generic project roadmap notes
notes: Primary regression for the recent BSQ derailment.

tasks.title: Minishell Parser Request Must Prefer Shell Context Over Project Meta
tasks.objective: Measure whether a minishell parser-design request pulls shell, parsing, and C notes instead of Project Index, README, or Roadmap notes.
tasks.prompt: Explain how to design a minimal command parser for minishell in C. Focus on tokenization, quotes, pipes, and redirections.
anti_signals: answers with roadmap or vision content
switches to unrelated C project structure
notes: Regression for focused coding retrieval where project meta notes used to dominate.

tasks.title: C Knowledge Gap Analysis Must Stay in the C Graph
tasks.objective: Measure whether a C note-gap analysis stays grounded in the existing Languages/C slice and proposes a missing C node instead of unrelated product or roadmap notes.
tasks.prompt: Analyze which C notes already exist and suggest one important missing node that should be added to the graph.
expected_signals: suggests one concrete missing c topic
keeps the answer in the c knowledge domain
notes: Regression for note-gap analysis contamination by unrelated project context.
